sermon.title: The Mystery of Extremes
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: From Ecclesiastes 7:18 and 1 Corinthians 13, Pastor David G. Kincer shows how six real truths—tongues, prophecy, knowledge, faith, giving to the poor, and giving the body to be burned—distract from God’s priority when taken to extremes. God is love, love is Christian maturity, love is as strong as death, and love never fails.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: One phrase at 6:00 was not clear. He says Pentecost was in “Acts chapter 1” (Acts 2), cites Romans 13:9 for the “love does no harm” verse (13:10), and says “verse 6” for 1 Corinthians 13:8. The 15 languages at Pentecost is his count. Sensitive content kept as spoken: the faith movement called a disaster, American churches and helping the poor, the Branch Davidians at Waco (sex with the congregation, asking them to die), graphic description of bodily decay in the grave.

chunks.short_answer: Love is what God is: good, wise, faithful, a judge of the guilty, no respecter of persons. Being unfaithful to a spouse or children, or failing to discipline your children, is not love. Maturity comes line upon line by prayer, Bible study and application.

chunks.short_answer: God gave his only begotten Son; our response is to worship and live for him. Judas did ministry yet lacked love. 1 Corinthians 13:8: love never fails, while prophecies fail, tongues cease and knowledge vanishes. Love is no harm to God, no harm to your neighbor, no harm to yourself.

All the wealth of his house it would be utterly despised. You can’t buy God. You can’t buy love. God gives it to us freely. By giving us himself. For God so loved the world that he gave his only what begotten son see his act of love was to come down and die for us and if we would believe that we would be forgiven and saved from our sins that’s his love. Our response to him is to worship him accept him and live for him that’s our love that’s our responsibility. Judas Iscariot he healed the sick he preached the gospel people got saved. He did all these things and he was a thief and he betrayed Christ.

God using him and others in the Bible had nothing to do with their Christian walk. Their faith it’s just God used them. And Judas Iscariot lacked love. And he went out and hung himself and killed himself after he realized what he did to Christ and so trying to work your way. Into brownie points with God isn’t it. Just have a love relationship with him. Don’t do anything to hurt God don’t do anything to hurt your family don’t do anything to hurt others and if you do admit it correct it and go on.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life.
Love never fails. But whether there are prophecies, they will fail; whether there are tongues, they will cease; whether there is knowledge, it will vanish away.

Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’

faqs.question: Is tongues the only sign of the Holy Ghost?
faqs.answer: No—he says the Bible doesn’t say that, and not everybody will speak in languages.

faqs.question: Are tongues biblical?
faqs.answer: Yes—just because others haven’t experienced them doesn’t mean they aren’t Bible; tongues and interpretation are a truth in the Bible.

faqs.question: Is taking medicine an act of unbelief?
faqs.answer: He calls that an irrational extreme of the faith camp.

faqs.question: Is praying more than once unbelief?
faqs.answer: No—Jesus prayed more than once, and he is our example.

faqs.question: What is Christian maturity?
faqs.answer: Love—not quoting scriptures, tongues, prophecy or healing; everybody can have it.

faqs.question: Can Christians drink?
faqs.answer: He says they can, but it violates a wise law of the Bible.

faqs.question: Is it loving not to discipline your children?
faqs.answer: No—God disciplines us, so failing to discipline your children is not love.

faqs.question: Can you buy God’s love?
faqs.answer: No—God gives it freely by giving us himself.

faqs.question: Did Judas do ministry?
faqs.answer: He says Judas healed the sick and preached, yet he was a thief who lacked love.

faqs.question: What is love, simply put?
faqs.answer: No harm to God, no harm to your neighbor, and no harm to yourself.
